passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Enacted bill text (Ch. 388) adding section 15-2401.01, which makes any resident eligible to enroll in public school a qualified student for an ESA; this page does not show Mathis's vote.

rows.reasoning: Mathis voted No on HB2853 (2022), a bill adding section 15-2401.01 to make ESA eligibility universal to any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school" who does not otherwise qualify. Per the annex, a lone No vote on an expansion bill is direction-only and does not by itself separate 'Opposing voucher programs and blocking their expansion, without moving to eliminate existing ones' (rung 2) from 'Eliminating voucher programs' (rung 1).
needs_source: Mathis's own words on whether existing Arizona ESA accounts should be repealed outright or merely capped from further expansion, to distinguish rung 1 from rung 2 following his No vote on HB2853.
